coverage_notes:
SOURCE BASIS. Two contemporaneous primary sources carried almost all of this: (1) LSU's own athletics-site staff directory archived mid-season, "2003 LSU Football Coaching/Strength Staff" (Wayback capture 2003-11-21), which is a clean HTML table of 16 names with exact position titles and years at LSU; and (2) the 2003 LSU Football Media Guide, archived on lsusports.net as page-range PDFs, whose "Football Support Staff" section (pp. 129-136) covers graduate assistants, interns, equipment, video, athletic training, and football operations. The archived athletics-wide "Equipment Staff" page (Wayback 2003-09-08) supplied the equipment tier and football student managers. 49 people total.

PDF QUOTE LIMITATION. Per instructions, every source that is a media-guide PDF has quote set to "" because the text cannot be copied faithfully. The 2003 guide's PDFs extract with pervasive intra-word letter-spacing artifacts (e.g. "B a r n e t t", "re c o rded", "ov e rall", "g raduate") and with role titles broken across lines, so any quote I copied would not string-match a re-extraction. For those rows the note gives the exact printed heading text, the PDF page range, and the printed page number. Where a clean HTML source also exists (the archived staff directory, the archived equipment page, Wikipedia, or a current official bio), I used that for the matchable quote and kept the PDF as corroboration.

HTML TABLE QUOTES. The archived staff-directory and equipment-staff pages are HTML tables where the name and the position sit in adjacent <td> cells, so no single contiguous string contains both. For those rows I supply two source entries per person - one quoting the Name cell verbatim, one quoting the Position cell verbatim - both from the same URL, with the pairing explained in the note.

WHAT IS FULLY COVERED. The complete on-field staff is recovered and internally consistent across both primary sources: Saban plus exactly nine assistants (Doll, Dooley, Fisher, Hixon, Travis Jones, Muschamp, Searels, Lance Thompson, Walton), which matches the NCAA limit of the era. Strength and conditioning, football operations/administration, video, athletic training, and equipment are all recovered by name and title.

WHAT IS PARTIAL OR UNCERTAIN.
- Graduate assistants and interns: the media guide documents four (Coley, Barnett, Scherer, Walker) and I recovered three more from secondary sources (Dawsey, Cochran, Mike Collins). This tier was not published as a roster in 2003, so I cannot assert the list is exhaustive; there were likely additional GAs and interns who were never printed anywhere I could find.
- Scott Cochran and Mike Collins do NOT appear on the official 2003-11-21 staff directory, which lists only four S&C staff (Moffitt, Bo Davis, Gadeken, Will Jones). Both are sourced to later retrospective bios (Wikipedia for Cochran; LSU's own 2004 staff bio for Collins). Their 2003 roles therefore sit below the tier LSU published, and Cochran's exact title in 2003 ("assistant strength and conditioning coach" per Wikipedia) conflicts with his absence from LSU's own contemporaneous S&C list - treat the title as approximate.
- Chad Walker role conflict: the 2003 media guide, written preseason, titles him "Recruiting Intern" and I used that verbatim with role_category ops. Wikipedia and later bios describe him as a defensive graduate assistant at LSU in 2003-2004. I kept the contemporaneous title and flagged the conflict in his source note; a consumer may prefer gradasst.
- Analysts and quality control: NOT RECOVERED, and I believe genuinely nonexistent as titled positions. No person on either primary source carries an "analyst" or "quality control" title; those roles had not yet proliferated in college football in 2003. The functional equivalents in this era were the graduate assistants (film breakdown, scouting reports - explicitly described in Coley's and Barnett's guide bios) and the video department. No row is categorized analyst or qc.
- Video staff: Doug Aucoin's guide bio states he "oversees a staff of eight people in the video department, which includes one full-time assistant, one graduate assistant and six student assistants." Only two of those eight are named (Aucoin, Fairburn). The video graduate assistant and six student assistants are UNRECOVERED - no source names them. I categorized the two named video staff as "other" rather than analyst, since Videography Director/Assistant Videographer are the titles as worded.
- Athletic training: the three named trainers (Marucci, Barker, Mullenix) are the football-relevant full-time staff per the media guide's Athletic Training Staff section. The guide elsewhere notes "Three full time trainers" plus "as many graduate assistants and student-trainers" - those GA and student trainers are UNRECOVERED. Team physicians are not named in any source I found and are NOT included.
- Equipment and student managers: the archived Equipment Staff page is athletics-wide, not football-only. I included the four full-time equipment staff (Boss, Shillings, Stringfellow, Boniol - the media guide's Equipment Staff section confirms all four work with football; Boniol's bio says he oversees Olympic sports "as well as working with the Tiger football team") and the twelve student managers whose Position cell explicitly says Football or Baseball/Football. Student managers are marked role_category equipment; a consumer wanting only salaried staff should filter these twelve out. Athletics-wide equipment staff without a football designation were excluded rather than guessed.
- Secretaries/receptionist (Spradley, CC Thompson, Stuckey) and the two operations coordinators (Mangum, Lofton) appear only as a name-and-title block on the last page of the guide's support-staff section, with no bio text. Names are as printed; "CC Thompson" is printed without periods, and "Ya'el Lofton" is printed with a typographic apostrophe.
- Wikipedia's 2003 LSU team page has no coaching-staff section; its navbox lists only assistants who happen to have Wikipedia articles, which is how Barnett, Cochran, Coley, Collins, Dawsey and Walker surfaced. It is not a staff roster and I did not treat it as one.
- Kirby Smart is frequently associated with this staff in popular retellings but joined LSU in 2004, not 2003. He is correctly EXCLUDED.

NO MID-SEASON MOVEMENT was documented for anyone. Every person listed is documented on staff for the 2003 season and, so far as any source shows, through the January 4, 2004 Sugar Bowl. No midseason_note was warranted on any row. Nothing in this dataset is inferred from plausibility - every row has a real source.
